attachment.content:
- academic-cv-builder: Format CVs for academic positions with publications, grants, and teaching
- animejs: Anime.js adapter patterns for HyperFrames. Use when writing Anime.js animations or timelines inside HyperFrames compositions, registering animations on window.__hfAnime, making Anime.js seek-driven and deterministic, or translating Anime.js examples into render-safe HyperFrames HTML.
- api-design: REST API design patterns including resource naming, status codes, pagination, filtering, error responses, versioning, and rate limiting for production APIs.
- application-form-filler: Fill out job application form fields with context-aware, tailored answers drawn from the candidate's CV and the job description
- aside-browser: Read when you need a browser, or have to work across user's logged-in websites (e.g. Gmail, Slack, cloud consoles, etc.), or have to refer personal contexts like memory and browsing history.
- backend-patterns: Backend architecture patterns, API design, database optimization, and server-side best practices for Node.js, Express, and Next.js API routes.
- career-changer-translator: Translate skills from one industry to another, identify transferable skills
- coding-standards: Universal coding standards, best practices, and patterns for TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and Node.js development.
- cold-email-writer: Write personalized cold outreach emails to hiring managers and founders — specific, human, not a pitch deck
- continuous-learning-v2: Instinct-based learning system that observes sessions via hooks, creates atomic instincts with confidence scoring, and evolves them into skills/commands/agents.
- cover-letter-generator: Create personalized, compelling cover letters from resume and job description
- creative-portfolio-resume: Balance visual design with ATS compatibility for creative roles
- css-animations: CSS animation adapter patterns for HyperFrames. Use when authoring CSS keyframes, animation-delay based timing, animation-fill-mode, animation-play-state, or CSS-only motion that HyperFrames must seek deterministically during preview and rendering.
- database-migrations: Database migration best practices for schema changes, data migrations, rollbacks, and zero-downtime deployments across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and common ORMs (Prisma, Drizzle, Django, TypeORM, golang-migrate).
- demo-video: Produce a short, polished product demo video (10–40s, with composed music + sound design) for a web app, site, or feature — autonomously, end to end, and re-renderable from the repo. Use when the user says "make a demo video", "promo/teaser/launch clip", "video for Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Product Hunt, a README", "show the product working", or shares a URL and wants video. Wraps HyperFrames (default) with a fast-pacing pipeline, real product data, procedurally composed music + synthesized SFX (no samples, no licenses) + local TTS narration with a warm-up ladder for "sounds robotic" feedback, and hard verification gates. Also covers the "record the real app with Playwright" path and when to pick Remotion instead.
- deployment-patterns: Deployment workflows, CI/CD pipeline patterns, Docker containerization, health checks, rollback strategies, and production readiness checklists for web applications.
- docker-patterns: Docker and Docker Compose patterns for local development, container security, networking, volume strategies, and multi-service orchestration.
- e2e-testing: Playwright E2E testing patterns, Page Object Model, configuration, CI/CD integration, artifact management, and flaky test strategies.
- eval-harness: Formal evaluation framework for Claude Code sessions implementing eval-driven development (EDD) principles
- executive-resume-writer: Create C-suite and VP level resumes emphasizing strategic leadership
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- frontend-patterns: Frontend development patterns for React, Next.js, state management, performance optimization, and UI best practices.
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- grill-me: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan or design until reaching shared understanding, resolving each branch of the decision tree. Use when user wants to stress-test a plan, get grilled on their design, or mentions "grill me".
- humanizer: Remove signs of AI-generated writing from text. Use when editing or reviewing
text to make it sound more natural and human-written. Based on Wikipedia's
comprehensive "Signs of AI writing" guide. Detects and fixes patterns including:
inflated symbolism, promotional language, superficial -ing analyses, vague
attributions, em dash overuse, rule of three, AI vocabulary words, negative
parallelisms, and excessive conjunctive phrases.
- hyperframes: Create video compositions, animations, title cards, overlays, captions, voiceovers, audio-reactive visuals, and scene transitions in HyperFrames HTML. Use when asked to build any HTML-based video content, add captions or subtitles synced to audio, generate text-to-speech narration, create audio-reactive animation (beat sync, glow, pulse driven by music), add animated text highlighting (marker sweeps, hand-drawn circles, burst lines, scribble, sketchout), or add transitions between scenes (crossfades, wipes, reveals, shader transitions). Covers composition authoring, timing, media, and the full video production workflow. For dev-loop CLI commands (init, lint, inspect, preview, render) see the hyperframes-cli skill; for asset preprocessing commands (tts, transcribe, remove-background) see the hyperframes-media skill.
- hyperframes-cli: HyperFrames CLI dev loop — `npx hyperframes` for scaffolding (init), validation (lint, inspect), preview, render, and environment troubleshooting (doctor, browser, info, upgrade). Use when running any of these commands or troubleshooting the HyperFrames build/render environment. For asset preprocessing commands (`tts`, `transcribe`, `remove-background`), invoke the `hyperframes-media` skill instead.
- hyperframes-media: Asset preprocessing for HyperFrames compositions — text-to-speech narration (Kokoro), audio/video transcription (Whisper), and background removal for transparent overlays (u2net). Use when generating voiceover from text, transcribing speech for captions, removing the background from a video or image to use as a transparent overlay, choosing a TTS voice or whisper model, or chaining these (TTS → transcribe → captions). Each command downloads its own model on first run.
- hyperframes-registry: Install and wire registry blocks and components into HyperFrames compositions. Use when running hyperframes add, installing a block or component, wiring an installed item into index.html, or working with hyperframes.json. Covers the add command, install locations, block sub-composition wiring, component snippet merging, and registry discovery.
- interview-prep-generator: Generate STAR stories, practice questions, and talking points from resume
- job-description-analyzer: Analyze job postings, calculate match scores, identify gaps, and create application strategy
- linkedin-profile-optimizer: Optimize LinkedIn profile for searchability, recruiter visibility, and engagement
- lottie: Lottie and dotLottie adapter patterns for HyperFrames. Use when embedding lottie-web JSON animations, .lottie files, @lottiefiles/dotlottie-web players, registering instances on window.__hfLottie, or making After Effects exports deterministic in HyperFrames.
- ml-check: Reviews ML code for correctness, reproducibility, and best practices
- offer-comparison-analyzer: Compare multiple job offers side-by-side with total compensation analysis
- orca-cli: Use the public `orca` CLI to operate Orca-managed worktrees, folder contexts, terminals, repos, automations, artifacts, skill sharing, worktree comments, and the browser embedded inside the Orca app. Use when the user says "$orca-cli", "use orca cli", "Orca worktree", "child worktree", "cardStatus", "spawn codex/claude in a worktree", "read/wait/send Orca terminal", "terminal send", "full handoff", "handover", "give this to another agent", "another worktree", "Orca browser", "orca artifacts", "share HTML/Markdown", "public artifact link", "share skills", or "control the browser inside Orca". Prefer this over raw `git worktree`, ad hoc PTYs, Playwright, or Computer Use when the task touches Orca-managed state. Use Computer Use for external browser windows, webviews, or desktop UI only when the task requires OS/window-level control such as focus, menus, dialogs, coordinates, or screenshots. Use `orca-cli` for Orca's embedded pages and a page-automation tool such as Playwright or CDP for external pages.
- orchestration: Use Orca orchestration for structured multi-agent coordination: threaded messages, blocking ask/reply flows, task dispatch, worker_done/escalation waits, task DAGs, decision gates, coordinator loops, or decomposing work across agents. # GitNexus — Code Intelligence

This project is indexed by GitNexus as **Agentic-Lagrangian-Extraction** (3666 symbols, 4246 relationships, 63 execution flows).

> Index stale? Run `node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze --index-only` from the project root — it auto-selects an available runner. No `.gitnexus/run.cjs` yet? Bootstrap with `npx`, `bunx`, or `pnpm dlx` — e.g. `bunx gitnexus@latest analyze` (npm 11 npx crash; #1939).

## Always Do

- **MUST run impact analysis before editing.** Use `impact({target: "symbolName", direction: "upstream"})` (MCP) or `node .gitnexus/run.cjs impact "symbolName" --direction upstream --repo .` (CLI fallback); report callers, processes, and risk. Never substitute grep for graph analysis.
- **MUST analyze graph changes before committing.** Use `detect_changes({scope: "all"})` (MCP) or `node .gitnexus/run.cjs detect-changes --scope all --repo .` (CLI fallback). `partial: true` or `truncated: true` is not a clean check — a zero means unseen, not unaffected; re-run it. For regression review: `detect_changes({scope: "compare", base_ref: "main"})` or `node .gitnexus/run.cjs detect-changes --scope compare --base-ref "main" --repo .`.
- **MUST warn the user** if impact analysis returns HIGH or CRITICAL risk before proceeding with edits.
- **MUST treat `risk: UNKNOWN` as unresolved, not as low.** An empty caller set is not evidence the symbol is unused — it can also mean the callers are not resolvable by the index (plain-object property access, dynamic dispatch, cross-language calls). `impact` pairs `UNKNOWN` with a `riskNote` saying so. Confirm with a text search before treating the symbol as safe to change or delete; do not proceed on the strength of a zero.
- When exploring unfamiliar code, use `query({search_query: "concept"})` to find execution flows instead of grepping. It returns process-grouped results ranked by relevance.
- When you need full context on a specific symbol — callers, callees, which execution flows it participates in — use `context({name: "symbolName"})`.
- For security review, `explain({target: "fileOrSymbol"})` lists taint findings (source→sink flows; needs `analyze --pdg`).

## Never Do

- NEVER edit a function, class, or method before MCP/CLI impact analysis.
- NEVER ignore HIGH or CRITICAL risk warnings from impact analysis, and never read `UNKNOWN` as an all-clear — it means the walk could not answer, which is the one verdict that requires confirming by other means.
- NEVER rename symbols with find-and-replace — use `rename` which understands the call graph.
- NEVER commit before MCP/CLI graph change analysis.

1	You are benchmarking automated extraction of a BSM physics model from its paper, to be compared against the physicist's own FeynRules implementation.

3	MODEL: 368sextets (SimpleExtensions) — FeynRules DB entry based on arXiv:2110.11359.
4	PAPER: full text at "/var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/rerun-368sextets-__sl7zst/eval/benchmark_runs/368sextets/text/2110.11359.txt" (read it with your file-reading tool; it is text extracted from the PDF; it is authoritative).

6	
7	TASK — extract the COMPLETE new-physics content:
8	1. Read the paper. Identify EVERY new particle beyond the Standard Model: spin (S/F/V), colour rep (singlet/triplet/sextet/octet), SU(2) rep, electric charge Q and/or hypercharge Y, mass parameter. COMPLETENESS IS SCORED — a model with several new states (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) must include all of them as separate ParticleClass entries (or class_members).
9	2. Identify the new coupling/mass/mixing parameters (External unless clearly derived).
10	3. Include the main new-physics lagrangian_terms (verbatim Mathematica strings, FeynRules idioms).
11	
12	SCHEMA RULES: all numeric physics values are STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on => gauge_groups []; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need NO declaration; any OTHER index (e.g. a colour-sextet index, a new-generation index) NEEDS an index_decls entry (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); every particle needs a unique class_index; self_conjugate=false for complex fields (distinct antiparticle), true for real/Majorana fields.
13	
14	OUTPUT: your FINAL message must contain exactly one fenced code block tagged json containing ONLY the FeynRulesModel JSON object (no commentary inside the fences). Set model_name to "368sextets_gen".
15	
16	SANDBOX: the sandbox root is /var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/rerun-368sextets-__sl7zst. It contains ONLY the paper, tools/frgen/frmodel.py
17	(the schema), tools/frgen/render.py (the renderer), and
18	tools/feynrules/test_files/models/SM.fr (the Standard Model file this add-on is loaded
19	on top of: take field names, index conventions and hypercharges from it). Nothing else
20	exists there and nothing outside /var/folders/pf/fm0v0g_52r754cfv3r4lqv980000gn/T/rerun-368sextets-__sl7zst may be read.
21	
22	## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)
23	
24	1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
25	   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
26	   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
27	   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
28	   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.
29	
30	2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.
31	
32	3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.
33	
34	4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.
35	
36	5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.
37	
38	6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.
39	
40	7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
41	   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
42	   - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
43	   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
44	   Never silently pick one placement.
45	
46	8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.
47	
48	## FeynRules and UFO construct rules (each one broke a compile or a MadGraph import in earlier runs)
49	
50	9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). Write covariant derivatives on the whole field, `DC[Phi, mu]`, never with an explicit colour index inside `DC[...]`.
51	
52	10. Names. Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...). No primes or punctuation in `ParticleName`/`AntiParticleName` (`W'` is not a valid UFO name; write `Wp`, `Wpbar`). Use class indices of 100 or more for new classes.
53	
54	11. Interaction orders. Every new coupling parameter (Yukawa, portal, quartic, new gauge coupling, dimensionless EFT coefficient) carries an `InteractionOrder`: `{NP, 1}` for a new-physics coupling, `{QED, 1}` or `{QCD, 1}` only when it is literally that coupling. Declare `M$InteractionOrderHierarchy` with every order you use (for example `{{QCD, 1}, {QED, 2}, {NP, 1}}`). A coupling with no order makes MadGraph reject the UFO ("Some couplings have '1' order").
55	
56	12. Tensor parameters. Give every indexed parameter explicit per-component values (`yN[1,1] -> 0.1, yN[1,2] -> 0, ...`; schema: `value_rules`). Never use a pattern rule such as `X[i_?NumericQ, j_?NumericQ] :> ...` in `Definitions`: FeynRules exports the pattern verbatim as a UFO parameter name and MadGraph fails with an unrelated "invalid syntax" error.
57	
58	13. Flavour structure in matrix form. Write generation-space couplings as matrix products between class fields, `uqbar.VCKMR.Ga[mu].ProjP.dq`, `LLbar.yN.NR`, `ISbar.Ga[mu].ProjM.IS`, not as explicit index sums `VCKMR[ff1, ff2] uqbar[ff1, cc]...dq[ff2, cc]`, and never nest one generation index inside another. Explicit-index forms leak FeynRules internals (`ConvertSpinToString`, `MakeIdenticalFermions`) into the UFO.
59	
60	14. One declared total. Define exactly one Lagrangian term named `LTotal` that sums every other term you define, and make sure every other term appears in that sum. Do not define two alternative totals. Do not emit a term that contains no field (a pure constant): FeynRules exports it as a vertex with no particles.
61	
62	15. Declarations. Every field used in a term is declared; every parameter used in a term is declared with a numeric default; every `SelfConjugate -> True` class has no `QuantumNumbers`; a Majorana mass term is `-1/2 M psibar.psi`.
63	
64	## Mandatory self-audit table (produce it BEFORE the model)
65	
66	For every Lagrangian term you emit, output one row of this table. Then fix any row that fails before you write the model.
67	
68	| term name | fields in the monomial | operator mass dimension d | coupling symbol | coupling mass dimension (must be 4 - d) | 1/Lambda power present (must be d - 4, or "n/a" if d <= 4) | Q sum | Y sum | SU(2) contraction (singlet? which Eps or shared index) | SU(3) contraction | sum of each new U(1) charge (one column per U(1), must be 0) | lepton/baryon number sum (if the paper assigns them) | CC[] used where paper writes psi^c (yes/no/n/a) | fraction/root placement checked against (equation, LaTeX line, or "n/a") | Hermitian partner (HC[] or self-conjugate) |
69	
70	Rules for the table:
71	- Field mass dimensions: scalar 1, vector 1, fermion 3/2, `FS[...]` 2, `del`/`DC` 1.
72	- Every Q sum, Y sum, and new-U(1) sum must equal 0. Use the charges you declared in `QuantumNumbers` and the SM.fr charges for SM fields. If a sum is not 0, the term is wrong; fix the contraction or the charge before you continue.
73	- If d > 4, the row must show `1/Lambda^(d-4)` and an External cutoff parameter, or a Description that states the absorbed dimension and units.
74	- Add one row per new particle class that confirms its kinetic + mass term exists and is in the total Lagrangian sum.
75	- Add one row per non-fundamental colour representation that confirms the `AddGaugeRepresentation[...]` line is present.
76	- Add one line under the table that lists every `SelfConjugate -> True` class and confirms it carries no `QuantumNumbers`.
77	- Add one line that lists every class, parameter and index name you chose and confirms none is a Mathematica built-in, a FeynRules symbol, or an SM.fr name.
78	- Add one line that names the single total Lagrangian and lists the terms it sums.
79	- Add one line that states whether any reference or cached model file was read (must be "none").

1	UCI-HEP-TR-2021-26
2	The phenomenological cornucopia of SU(3) exotica
3	Linda M. Carpenter∗and Taylor Murphy†
4	Department of Physics, The Ohio State University
5	191 W. WoodruﬀAve., Columbus, OH 43212, U.S.A.
6	Tim M. P. Tait‡
7	Department of Physics and Astronomy,
8	University of California, Irvine
9	Irvine, CA 92697, U.S.A.
10	(Dated: September 9, 2022)
11	We introduce an eﬀort to catalog the gauge-invariant interactions of Standard Model (SM) particles and new
12	ﬁelds in a variety of representations of the SM color gauge group SU(3)c. In this ﬁrst installment, we direct
13	this eﬀort toward ﬁelds in the six-dimensional (sextet, 6) representation. We consider eﬀective operators of
14	mass dimension up to seven (comprehensively up to dimension six), featuring both scalar and fermionic color
15	sextets. We use an iterative tensor-product method to identify the color invariants underpinning such operators,
16	emphasizing structures that have received little attention to date. In order to demonstrate the utility of our approach,
17	we study a simple but novel model of color-sextet ﬁelds at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). We compute cross
18	sections for an array of new production channels enabled by our operators, including single-sextet production and
19	sextet production in association with photons or leptons. We also discuss dĳet-resonance constraints on a sextet
20	fermion. This example shows that there remains a wide array of fairly minimal but well motivated and unexplored
21	models with extended strong sectors as we await the high-luminosity LHC.
22	I.
23	INTRODUCTION
24	The search for physics beyond the Standard Model (bSM),
25	spearheaded by the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC) [1],
26	continues unabated, spurred on by a constellation of theoreti-
27	cal deﬁciencies and experimental anomalies that continue to
28	bedevil the Standard Model. These issues range from the well
29	known naturalness problems [2–5] to the collection of persistent
30	muon [6] and ﬂavor anomalies [7, 8] and the ongoing search for
31	particle dark matter [9, 10]. While there exist a wide variety
32	of speciﬁc, sometimes ultraviolet-complete, frameworks that
33	seek to rectify some or all of the Standard Model’s shortcom-
34	ings, some — in the absence of experimental evidence for any
35	speciﬁc bSM model — have turned to an eﬀective ﬁeld theory
36	(EFT) approach to study new physics in a simpliﬁed and more
37	model-independent manner.
38	The EFT approach, which in the simplest terms allows one
39	to study the experimentally accessible degrees of freedom in
40	a theory while remaining agnostic about physics at higher
41	energy scales, has been used to great eﬀect in many contexts.
42	Some pertinent examples include the Standard Model Eﬀective
43	Field Theory (SMEFT) [11], which now includes (in at least
44	one basis) every independent operator comprising SM ﬁelds
45	of up to mass dimension eight [12–14] and has lately been
46	used to probe experimental anomalies; and the variety of
47	eﬀective operators employed in supersymmetric frameworks
48	in which supersymmetry breaking is communicated by heavy
49	messengers from a hidden sector to the visible world [15, 16].
50	Lying somewhere between the SMEFT and supersym-
51	metric models on the scale of bSM theories ranked by ex-
52	∗lmc@physics.osu.edu
53	† murphy.1573@osu.edu
54	‡ ttait@uci.edu
55	otic particle content are simpliﬁed models in which the
56	SM is augmented only by new matter whose only non-
57	trivial gauge transformations are under the SM gauge group
58	GSM = SU(3)c × SU(2)L × U(1)𝑌. A particularly simple but
59	fruitful subset of these models feature a new color-charged
60	SU(2)L singlet perhaps with non-vanishing weak hypercharge.
61	While new color-charged ﬁelds — particularly SU(3)c triplets
62	and octets (adjoints) — occur in a panoply of bSM theories and
63	have long been studied in those speciﬁc contexts, there has been
64	far less attempt at a coherent and comprehensive accounting of
65	bSM strong interactions in an EFT framework. We intend to
66	address this gap in the literature, beginning with the present
67	work.
68	We construct a catalog of eﬀective operators governing
69	ﬁelds in the six-dimensional (sextet) representation of SU(3)c,
70	which remain hypothetical but can be copiously produced in
71	proton-proton (𝑝𝑝) collisions and are therefore highly relevant
72	to the ongoing LHC program. Using an iterative tensor-product
73	method to construct new color invariants, we enumerate all
74	possible operators of mass dimension up to six connecting
75	sextets to Standard Model ﬁelds, and additionally identify a
76	few potentially interesting dimension-seven operators. Several
77	of these operators have to date received little or no attention.
78	In order to motivate this operator catalog ex post facto, we
79	construct two simpliﬁed models of color-sextet ﬁelds and
80	explore the phenomenology of these particles at the LHC.
81	These models are notably diﬀerent from previous models of
82	color sextets in that the novel particles couple not to quark pairs,
83	like the aptly named “sextet diquarks” [17–19], but instead to
84	a quark and a gluon. We ﬁnd fairly light constraints on sextet
85	fermions from a CMS search for dĳet resonances [20] and
86	propose future searches for the other interesting multĳet + 𝛾/𝑍
87	or lepton signatures generated by these simple models.
88	This paper is organized as follows. In Section II, we show
89	how to build a catalog of exotic-color operators starting from
90	arXiv:2110.11359v3  [hep-ph]  7 Sep 2022
91	
92	
93	2
94	ﬁrst principles, and we produce such a catalog for color-sextet
95	ﬁelds. In Section III, we use a small subset of these operators to
96	explore a simpliﬁed model of color-sextet scalars and fermions.
97	We compute cross sections for a variety of production modes
98	and discuss LHC phenomenology while surveying constraints
99	on these novel particles. Section IV concludes. The appendix
100	contains a thorough discussion of the representation theory of
101	the SU(3) sextet, along with some notes about the implemen-

1267	Cross sections and LHC signatures
1268	At a high-energy hadron collider, color sextets can be pro-
1269	duced in pairs (predominantly through their SU(3)c gauge
1270	interactions) as well as singly, often in association with SM
1271	leptons or gauge bosons. Representative diagrams for pair
1272	production are displayed in Figure 1 and proceed via gluon
1273	fusion and quark-antiquark annihilation. Contributions to Ψ ¯Ψ
1274	production from the higher dimensional operators in (12) are
1275	typically negligible for reasonable choices of ΛΨ𝑞. The cross
1276	sections of sextet fermion and scalar pair production at the LHC
1277	with √𝑠= 13 TeV are displayed in Figure 2, with systematic
1278	errors estimated by adding the scale and PDF variations re-
1279	ported by MG5_aMC in quadrature. Because pair production
1280	is dominated by gauge interactions, the cross sections are not
1281	only essentially independent of 𝜅𝐼
1282	𝑞and ΛΨ𝑞, but are also nearly
1283	identical for sextets coupling to up- and down-type quarks. The
1284	spin of the sextet is important, with the scalar cross section(s)
1285	hovering a bit less than an order of magnitude below those of
1286	the fermions. All cross sections are of O(1–10) pb for masses
1287	below the TeV scale but fall quite steeply with increasing sextet
1288	mass. It is worth noting that these results are consistent with
1289	the small existing literature for sextet fermions [31, 32] and
1290	scalars [18, 19, 33].

1680	IV.
1681	CONCLUSIONS
1682	In this work we have taken a new look at the possible interac-
1683	tions of beyond-the-Standard Model particles that are charged
1684	under the SM color gauge group SU(3)c. Such states can be co-
1685	piously produced at the LHC, and it is important to understand
1686	the space of their possible interactions in order to understand
1687	how LHC data constrains their existence. In this work, we
1688	have explored the gauge-invariant interactions of ﬁelds in the
1689	six-dimensional (sextet) representation of SU(3)c, producing a
1690	(large) catalog of operators, many of which have received little

1694	or no attention in the literature to date but may produce distinct
1695	phenomenology worthy of investigation. We have focused
1696	on color sextets in this work because they transform in the
1697	lowest-dimensional representation of SU(3)c not yet observed
1698	in Nature. We have speciﬁcally focused on higher-dimensional
1699	interactions linking color-sextet fermions and scalars to a SM
1700	quark and a gluon (and possibly additional particles), com-
1701	puting cross sections for a variety of production modes and
1702	surveying existing LHC constraints on these particles.
1703	Much of what we have done here is intended to set up future
1704	work. On one hand, one could undertake a much more thorough
1705	investigation of the speciﬁc color-sextet models we introduced
1706	above; such a study could compute next-to-leading order (NLO)
1707	corrections within the EFT framework or could propose an
1708	ultraviolet completion for one or more of the operators we
1709	consider7. It could also be worthwhile to rigorously compute
1710	sensitivity projections for any of the non-standard signatures
1711	we described in Section III.B at the high-luminosity LHC. Such
1712	projections would be derived from a tailored selection strategy,
1713	which would be interesting to develop. It would also be natural
1714	to complete the color-sextet operator catalog at mass dimension
1715	seven, or to allow for extended sectors comprising sextets with
1716	distinct weak hypercharges or non-trivial transformations under
1717	SU(2)L.
1718	On the other hand, as we hopefully have demonstrated with
1719	the example of color sextets, the method we have employed
1720	to build our operator catalog can be used to build a variety of
1721	phenomenological models containing higher representations
1722	of SU(3)c. Similar catalogs could be built for other representa-
1723	tions, including the more frequently studied triplets and octets
1724	but also higher-dimensional ﬁelds; we plan to investigate sev-
1725	eral such catalogs going forward. The interactions we unearth
1726	in these catalogs could also be embedded in richer or more
1727	complete theories, for instance via the incorporation of a SM
1728	gauge singlet as a dark matter candidate.

1	"""
2	# frmodel.py is a part of the HEPTAPOD package.
3	# Copyright (C) 2025 HEPTAPOD authors (see AUTHORS for details).
4	# HEPTAPOD is licensed under the GNU GPL v3 or later, see LICENSE for details.
5	# Please respect the MCnet Guidelines, see GUIDELINES for details.
6	
7	Structured schema for a FeynRules ``.fr`` model file.
8	
9	This is the shared representation produced by Lagrangian extraction and consumed
10	by the ``.fr`` generator (render.py). Design principle: STRUCTURE the regular,
11	error-prone blocks (M$Parameters, M$ClassesDescription, M$GaugeGroups,
12	M$Information, IndexRange) so an LLM never hand-writes their Mathematica syntax,
13	and CARRY the irregular parts (Lagrangian algebra, mixing blocks, NLO
14	bookkeeping) as verbatim Mathematica strings.
15	
16	All numeric fields are strings so exact FeynRules syntax survives untouched:
17	rationals like ``-1/3``, decimals like ``1500.``, scientific ``2.5*^-3``.
18	"""
19	
20	from __future__ import annotations
21	
22	import re
23	from enum import Enum
24	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union
25	
26	from pydantic import BaseModel, model_validator
27	
28	# A verbatim numeric string: "-1/3", "1500.", "2.5*^-3", "Internal", "Automatic".
29	NumberStr = str
30	
31	
32	class Rule(BaseModel):
33	    """One Mathematica replacement rule, e.g. ``CKM[1,2] -> Sin[cabi]``."""
34	
35	    lhs: str
36	    rhs: str
37	    delayed: bool = False  # False -> "->", True -> ":>"
38	
39	    def render(self) -> str:
40	        return f"{self.lhs} {':>' if self.delayed else '->'} {self.rhs}"
41	
42	
43	class ParamType(str, Enum):
44	    External = "External"
45	    Internal = "Internal"
46	
47	
48	class SpinType(str, Enum):
49	    S = "S"  # scalar
50	    F = "F"  # fermion
51	    V = "V"  # vector
52	    U = "U"  # ghost
53	    T = "T"  # tensor
54	    W = "W"  # Weyl fermion
55	    R = "R"  # spin-3/2
56	    RW = "RW"
57	
58	
59	class RangeKind(str, Enum):
60	    Unfold = "Unfold"
61	    NoUnfold = "NoUnfold"
62	    Range = "Range"
63	
64	
65	class PropType(str, Enum):
66	    Sine = "Sine"
67	    Straight = "Straight"
68	    ScalarDash = "ScalarDash"
69	    GhostDash = "GhostDash"
70	    Curly = "Curly"
71	    W = "W"
72	    C = "C"
73	    S = "S"
74	    D = "D"
75	
76	
77	class PropArrow(str, Enum):
78	    true = "True"
79	    false = "False"
80	    none = "None"
81	    forward = "Forward"
82	
83	
84	class ModelInfo(BaseModel):
85	    authors: List[str]
86	    version: str
87	    date: str
88	    institutions: List[str] = []
89	    emails: List[str] = []
90	
91	
92	class GaugeGroup(BaseModel):
93	    """A M$GaugeGroups entry. Omitted entirely by BSM add-on models."""
94	
95	    name: str  # LHS symbol: U1Y, SU2L, SU3C
96	    abelian: bool
97	    gauge_boson: str
98	    coupling_constant: Optional[str] = None
99	    charge: Optional[str] = None  # required iff abelian
100	    structure_constant: Optional[str] = None  # required iff non-abelian
101	    symmetric_tensor: Optional[str] = None
102	    representations: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # [("T","Colour")] or many
103	    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM rule strings
104	
105	    @model_validator(mode="after")
106	    def _check(self) -> "GaugeGroup":
107	        if self.abelian and not self.charge:
108	            raise ValueError(f"gauge group {self.name}: Abelian group needs charge")
109	        if not self.abelian and not self.structure_constant:
110	            raise ValueError(
111	                f"gauge group {self.name}: non-Abelian group needs structure_constant"
112	            )
113	        return self
114	
115	
116	class IndexDecl(BaseModel):
117	    name: str  # Colour, Generation, SU2W ...
118	    range_kind: RangeKind
119	    size: int  # Range[size]
120	    style_symbol: Optional[str] = None  # IndexStyle[name, style_symbol]
121	
122	
123	class Parameter(BaseModel):
124	    """A M$Parameters entry (LHS symbol of ``==``)."""
125	
126	    name: str
127	    parameter_type: Optional[ParamType] = None
128	    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # scalar; tensors use value_rules
129	    value_rules: List[Rule] = []  # tensor Value -> { ... }
130	    complex: Optional[bool] = None  # ComplexParameter
131	    block_name: Optional[str] = None  # External only
132	    order_block: Optional[int] = None  # External SCALAR only
133	    interaction_order: Optional[Tuple[str, int]] = None  # -> {NP, 1}
134	    indices: List[str] = []  # non-empty => tensor
135	    definitions: List[Rule] = []
136	    parameter_name: Optional[str] = None
137	    tex: Optional[str] = None
138	    description: Optional[str] = None
139	    tensor_class: Optional[str] = None
140	    # tensor-only flags
141	    unitary: Optional[bool] = None
142	    hermitian: Optional[bool] = None
143	    orthogonal: Optional[bool] = None
144	    allow_summation: Optional[bool] = None
145	
146	    @property
147	    def is_tensor(self) -> bool:
148	        return bool(self.indices)
149	
150	    @model_validator(mode="after")
151	    def _check(self) -> "Parameter":
152	        if self.is_tensor:
153	            if self.value is not None:
154	                raise ValueError(
155	                    f"parameter {self.name}: tensor uses value_rules, not scalar value"
156	                )
157	            if self.order_block is not None:
158	                raise ValueError(
159	                    f"parameter {self.name}: order_block forbidden on tensors"
160	                )
161	        exclusive = [f for f in (self.unitary, self.hermitian, self.orthogonal) if f]
162	        if len(exclusive) > 1:
163	            raise ValueError(
164	                f"parameter {self.name}: at most one of unitary/hermitian/orthogonal"
165	            )
166	        if (self.unitary or self.hermitian) and self.complex is False:
167	            raise ValueError(
168	                f"parameter {self.name}: unitary/hermitian require complex=True"
169	            )
170	        if self.orthogonal and self.complex is True:
171	            raise ValueError(f"parameter {self.name}: orthogonal must be real")
172	        if self.parameter_type == ParamType.External and self.complex is True:
173	            raise ValueError(
174	                f"parameter {self.name}: External params must be real "
175	                "(split into real/imag or make Internal)"
176	            )
177	        return self
178	
179	
180	class MassSpec(BaseModel):
181	    """Renders 0 | {sym} | {sym,val} | {sym,Internal} | {gen,{m1,v1},...}."""
182	
183	    massless: bool = False  # -> literal 0
184	    sym: Optional[str] = None
185	    value: Optional[NumberStr] = None  # number | "Internal" | "Automatic" | None
186	    members: List[Tuple[str, Optional[NumberStr]]] = []  # multi-gen
187	
188	    @model_validator(mode="after")
189	    def _check(self) -> "MassSpec":
190	        if not self.massless and not self.sym:
191	            raise ValueError("MassSpec needs massless=True or a sym")
192	        return self
193	
194	
195	class ParticleClass(BaseModel):
196	    """A M$ClassesDescription entry, e.g. ``S[100] == {...}``."""
197	
198	    spin_type: SpinType
199	    class_index: int  # the n in S[100]
200	    class_name: str
201	    self_conjugate: bool
202	    indices: List[str] = []  # -> Index[...] wrapped
203	    flavor_index: Optional[str] = None  # BARE name
204	    class_members: List[str] = []
205	    mass: Optional[MassSpec] = None
206	    width: Optional[MassSpec] = None
207	    quantum_numbers: Dict[str, NumberStr] = {}  # values are strings -> preserve -1/3
208	    pdg: Optional[Union[int, List[int]]] = None
209	    particle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
210	    antiparticle_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
211	    full_name: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
212	    propagator_label: Optional[Union[str, List[str]]] = None
213	    propagator_type: Optional[PropType] = None
214	    propagator_arrow: Optional[PropArrow] = None
215	    unphysical: bool = False
216	    definitions: List[str] = []  # VERBATIM Mathematica rule strings
217	    ghost: Optional[str] = None  # U[n] only
218	    goldstone: Optional[str] = None  # S[n] only
219	    weyl_components: List[str] = []
220	    majorana_phase: Optional[str] = None
221	    chirality: Optional[str] = None
222	
223	    @property
224	    def class_label(self) -> str:
225	        return f"{self.spin_type.value}[{self.class_index}]"
226	
227	    @model_validator(mode="after")
228	    def _check(self) -> "ParticleClass":
229	        if self.unphysical:
230	            if self.mass or self.pdg:
231	                raise ValueError(
232	                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields omit mass/pdg"
233	                )
234	            if not self.definitions:
235	                raise ValueError(
236	                    f"particle {self.class_name}: unphysical fields require definitions"
237	                )
238	        if len(self.class_members) > 1:
239	            if not self.flavor_index:
240	                raise ValueError(
241	                    f"particle {self.class_name}: multi-member class needs flavor_index"
242	                )
243	            n = len(self.class_members)
244	            for lst in (
245	                self.pdg,
246	                self.particle_name,
247	                self.antiparticle_name,
248	                self.full_name,
249	            ):
250	                if isinstance(lst, list) and len(lst) != n:
251	                    raise ValueError(
252	                        f"particle {self.class_name}: list length must equal "
253	                        f"member count ({n})"
254	                    )
255	        if self.spin_type == SpinType.U:
256	            if self.self_conjugate:
257	                raise ValueError(
258	                    f"particle {self.class_name}: ghosts must be self_conjugate=False"
259	                )
260	            if not self.ghost:
261	                raise ValueError(f"particle {self.class_name}: ghost needs ghost=<boson>")
262	        return self
263	
264	
265	class LagrangianTerm(BaseModel):
266	    name: str  # LHS symbol
267	    expression: str  # VERBATIM Mathematica RHS
268	    delayed: bool = False  # True -> ":=", False -> "="
269	
270	
271	def _references(text: str, name: str) -> bool:
272	    """True if ``name`` appears in ``text`` as a whole Mathematica token."""
273	    if not text:
274	        return False
275	    return re.search(rf"(?<![A-Za-z0-9$]){re.escape(name)}(?![A-Za-z0-9$])", text) is not None
276	
277	
278	def _param_refs(p: Parameter, names: set) -> set:
279	    """Names of other parameters referenced by ``p``'s value/rules/definitions."""
280	    texts: List[str] = []
281	    if p.value:
282	        texts.append(p.value)
283	    for r in p.value_rules:
284	        texts.append(r.rhs)
285	    for r in p.definitions:
286	        texts.append(r.rhs)
287	    blob = " ".join(texts)
288	    return {n for n in names if n != p.name and _references(blob, n)}
289	
290	
291	def topo_sort_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> List[Parameter]:
292	    """Order parameters so each is defined before others that reference it.
293	
294	    Stable (preserves input order among independent params). Raises on a
295	    dependency cycle.
296	    """
297	    names = {p.name for p in params}
298	    deps = {p.name: _param_refs(p, names) for p in params}
299	    by_name = {p.name: p for p in params}
300	
301	    ordered: List[Parameter] = []
302	    emitted: set = set()
303	    remaining = [p.name for p in params]  # preserve input order
304	
305	    while remaining:
306	        progressed = False
307	        still: List[str] = []
308	        for n in remaining:
309	            if deps[n] <= emitted:
310	                ordered.append(by_name[n])
311	                emitted.add(n)
312	                progressed = True
313	            else:
314	                still.append(n)
315	        remaining = still
316	        if not progressed:
317	            raise ValueError(
318	                f"cyclic parameter dependency among: {sorted(remaining)}"
319	            )
320	    return ordered
321	
322	
323	class FeynRulesModel(BaseModel):
324	    """A complete FeynRules ``.fr`` model, ready to render."""
325	
326	    model_name: str
327	    info: ModelInfo
328	    interaction_order_hierarchy: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
329	    interaction_order_limit: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
330	    feynman_gauge: Optional[bool] = None
331	    vevs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # {{Phi[..], vev}}
332	    gauge_groups: List[GaugeGroup] = []
333	    index_decls: List[IndexDecl] = []
334	    parameters: List[Parameter] = []
335	    particles: List[ParticleClass] = []
336	    gauge_xi: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []  # (V[3], "GaugeXi[W]")
337	    lagrangian_terms: List[LagrangianTerm] = []
338	    # Verbatim escape hatches for irregular constructs (FR$LoopSwitches,
339	    # Mix[...] mixing blocks, SUSY superfields, ...).
340	    raw_preamble: List[str] = []  # emitted after M$Information, before IndexRange
341	    raw_blocks: List[str] = []  # emitted just before Lagrangian terms
342	
343	    @model_validator(mode="after")
344	    def _check(self) -> "FeynRulesModel":
345	        labels = [p.class_label for p in self.particles]
346	        if len(labels) != len(set(labels)):
347	            dupes = sorted({x for x in labels if labels.count(x) > 1})
348	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate ParticleClass labels: {dupes}")
349	
350	        # Lorentz/Spin* are FeynRules built-ins. Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/
351	        # SU2W are declared by SM.fr, which every BSM add-on is loaded on top of,
352	        # so they need no IndexRange in the add-on itself (matches the reference
353	        # S1_LQ_RR.fr, which uses Index[Colour] without redeclaring it). Only
354	        # genuinely new indices must be declared in index_decls.
355	        builtin = {
356	            "Lorentz", "Spin", "Spin1", "Spin2",
357	            "Colour", "Gluon", "Generation", "SU2D", "SU2W",
358	        }
359	        declared = {d.name for d in self.index_decls} | builtin
360	        used = {i for p in self.particles for i in p.indices} | {
361	            i for prm in self.parameters for i in prm.indices
362	        }
363	        missing = used - declared
364	        if missing:
365	            raise ValueError(
366	                f"indices used without an IndexRange declaration: {sorted(missing)}"
367	            )
368	
369	        self.parameters = topo_sort_parameters(self.parameters)
370	        return self
371

1	"""
2	# render.py is a part of the HEPTAPOD package.
3	# Copyright (C) 2025 HEPTAPOD authors (see AUTHORS for details).
4	# HEPTAPOD is licensed under the GNU GPL v3 or later, see LICENSE for details.
5	# Please respect the MCnet Guidelines, see GUIDELINES for details.
6	
7	Render a validated FeynRulesModel (frmodel.py) to a FeynRules ``.fr`` file.
8	
9	The fiddly Mathematica syntax (association comma placement, ``->`` vs ``:>``,
10	mass tuples, ``Index[...]`` wrapping, rationals) is built here in tested Python;
11	a thin Jinja2 template (templates/model.fr.j2) supplies the file skeleton.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import os
17	from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
18	
19	from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape
20	
21	from .frmodel import (
22	    FeynRulesModel,
23	    GaugeGroup,
24	    IndexDecl,
25	    MassSpec,
26	    Parameter,
27	    ParticleClass,
28	)
29	
30	_TEMPLATE_DIR = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "templates")
31	
32	
33	# --------------------------- scalar helpers --------------------------- #
34	
35	
36	def _bool(b: bool) -> str:
37	    return "True" if b else "False"
38	
39	
40	def _quote(s: str) -> str:
41	    return '"' + s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
42	
43	
44	def _strlist(items: Sequence[str]) -> str:
45	    """M$Information-style: single -> "x"; many -> {"x", "y"}."""
46	    if len(items) == 1:
47	        return _quote(items[0])
48	    return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in items) + "}"
49	
50	
51	def _name_field(v) -> str:
52	    """ParticleName/FullName/PropagatorLabel: str -> quoted; list -> {...}."""
53	    if isinstance(v, list):
54	        return "{" + ", ".join(_quote(x) for x in v) + "}"
55	    return _quote(v)
56	
57	
58	def _pdg(v) -> str:
59	    if isinstance(v, list):
60	        return "{" + ", ".join(str(x) for x in v) + "}"
61	    return str(v)
62	
63	
64	def _indices(names: Sequence[str]) -> str:
65	    return "{" + ", ".join(f"Index[{n}]" for n in names) + "}"
66	
67	
68	# FeynRules QuantumNumbers holds only additive (U(1)-type) charges. Colour/SU2/
69	# etc. are REPRESENTATION labels fixed by a field's Indices, not quantum numbers;
70	# if left in QuantumNumbers, FeynRules emits an unevaluated `Colour[field]` into
71	# the UFO's particles.py, which MadGraph rejects with "name 'Colour' is not
72	# defined". Drop these reserved index/representation names.
73	_REP_LABELS = {
74	    "Colour", "Color", "Sextet", "Gluon", "Generation", "Spin", "Lorentz",
75	    "SU2", "SU2W", "SU2L", "SU2D", "SU2R",
76	}
77	
78	
79	def _additive_qns(d: dict) -> dict:
80	    return {k: v for k, v in d.items() if k not in _REP_LABELS}
81	
82	
83	def _reserved_mass_width_names(particles) -> set:
84	    """Mass/width parameter names FeynRules auto-declares from particle Mass/Width
85	    specs. Declaring them again in M$Parameters double-defines the name in the UFO
86	    (MadGraph InvalidModel), so the renderer drops those duplicates."""
87	    names: set = set()
88	    for p in particles or []:
89	        for spec in (getattr(p, "mass", None), getattr(p, "width", None)):
90	            if spec is None:
91	                continue
92	            if getattr(spec, "sym", None):
93	                names.add(spec.sym)
94	            for sub, _val in (getattr(spec, "members", None) or []):
95	                names.add(sub)
96	    return names
97	
98	
99	def _is_internal_param(p) -> bool:
100	    """Internal/derived parameters carry a formula (Definitions) that FeynRules
101	    cannot auto-create from a particle Mass/Width spec, so they must stay in
102	    M$Parameters even when named like a mass/width (e.g. a computed decay width
103	    Width -> {WV1, Internal}). Only plain External duplicates are dropped."""
104	    if getattr(p, "definitions", None):
105	        return True
106	    return "internal" in str(getattr(p, "parameter_type", "")).lower()
107	
108	
109	def _qn(d: dict) -> str:
110	    return "{" + ", ".join(f"{k} -> {v}" for k, v in _additive_qns(d).items()) + "}"
111	
112	
113	def _interaction_order(t: Tuple[str, int]) -> str:
114	    return f"{{{t[0]}, {t[1]}}}"
115	
116	
117	def _mw_value(v):
118	    """Normalize a mass/width value. FeynRules' ``Automatic`` width is computed
119	    only when AddDecays is on — which is off for us (broken on Wolfram >=15), so
120	    it leaks the literal ``Automatic`` into the UFO and MadGraph fails with
121	    ``name 'Automatic' is not defined``. Emit a numeric placeholder instead;
122	    MadGraph's compute_widths recovers the real width from the model."""
123	    return "1." if str(v).strip().lower() == "automatic" else v
124	
125	
126	def _mass(m: MassSpec) -> str:
127	    if m.massless:
128	        return "0"
129	    if m.members:
130	        parts = [m.sym]
131	        for sub, val in m.members:
132	            val = _mw_value(val)
133	            parts.append(f"{{{sub}, {val}}}" if val is not None else f"{{{sub}}}")
134	        return "{" + ", ".join(parts) + "}"
135	    if m.value is not None:
136	        return f"{{{m.sym}, {_mw_value(m.value)}}}"
137	    return f"{{{m.sym}}}"
138	
139	
140	def _reps(reps: Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
141	    if len(reps) == 1:
142	        r, s = reps[0]
143	        return f"{{{r}, {s}}}"
144	    return "{" + ", ".join(f"{{{r}, {s}}}" for r, s in reps) + "}"
145	
146	
147	def _assoc(pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]], indent: str = "    ") -> str:
148	    """Render ``{ Key -> val, ... }``, dropping entries whose value is None."""
149	    kept = [(k, v) for k, v in pairs if v is not None]
150	    if not kept:
151	        return "{}"
152	    inner = ",\n".join(f"{indent}{k} -> {v}" for k, v in kept)
153	    close_indent = indent[:-2] if len(indent) >= 2 else ""
154	    return "{\n" + inner + "\n" + close_indent + "}"
155	
156	
157	# ------------------------------ blocks ------------------------------- #
158	
159	
160	def render_information(info) -> str:
161	    pairs = [
162	        ("Authors", _strlist(info.authors)),
163	        ("Version", _quote(info.version)),
164	        ("Date", _quote(info.date)),
165	        ("Institutions", _strlist(info.institutions) if info.institutions else None),
166	        ("Emails", _strlist(info.emails) if info.emails else None),
167	    ]
168	    return "M$Information = " + _assoc(pairs, indent="  ") + ";"
169	
170	
171	def _render_gauge_group(g: GaugeGroup) -> str:
172	    pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
173	        ("Abelian", _bool(g.abelian)),
174	        ("CouplingConstant", g.coupling_constant),
175	        ("GaugeBoson", g.gauge_boson),
176	        ("Charge", g.charge),
177	        ("StructureConstant", g.structure_constant),
178	        ("Representations", _reps(g.representations) if g.representations else None),
179	        ("SymmetricTensor", g.symmetric_tensor),
180	        (
181	            "Definitions",
182	            ("{" + ", ".join(g.definitions) + "}") if g.definitions else None,
183	        ),
184	    ]
185	    return f"  {g.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
186	
187	
188	def render_gauge_groups(groups: List[GaugeGroup]) -> str:
189	    entries = ",\n".join(_render_gauge_group(g) for g in groups)
190	    return "M$GaugeGroups = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
191	
192	
193	def render_index_decls(decls: List[IndexDecl]) -> str:
194	    lines: List[str] = []
195	    for d in decls:
196	        if d.range_kind.value == "Range":
197	            rng = f"Range[{d.size}]"
198	        else:
199	            rng = f"{d.range_kind.value}[Range[{d.size}]]"
200	        lines.append(f"IndexRange[Index[{d.name}]] = {rng};")
201	    for d in decls:
202	        if d.style_symbol:
203	            lines.append(f"IndexStyle[{d.name}, {d.style_symbol}];")
204	    return "\n".join(lines)
205	
206	
207	def _render_parameter(p: Parameter) -> str:
208	    pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
209	        ("ParameterType", p.parameter_type.value if p.parameter_type else None),
210	    ]
211	    if p.is_tensor:
212	        pairs.append(
213	            (
214	                "Value",
215	                ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.value_rules) + "}")
216	                if p.value_rules
217	                else None,
218	            )
219	        )
220	        pairs.append(("Indices", _indices(p.indices)))
221	    else:
222	        pairs.append(("Value", p.value))
223	    pairs += [
224	        ("ComplexParameter", _bool(p.complex) if p.complex is not None else None),
225	        ("BlockName", p.block_name),
226	        ("OrderBlock", str(p.order_block) if p.order_block is not None else None),
227	        (
228	            "InteractionOrder",
229	            _interaction_order(p.interaction_order) if p.interaction_order else None,
230	        ),
231	        (
232	            "Definitions",
233	            ("{" + ", ".join(r.render() for r in p.definitions) + "}")
234	            if p.definitions
235	            else None,
236	        ),
237	        ("ParameterName", p.parameter_name),
238	        ("TensorClass", p.tensor_class),
239	        ("Unitary", _bool(p.unitary) if p.unitary is not None else None),
240	        ("Hermitian", _bool(p.hermitian) if p.hermitian is not None else None),
241	        ("Orthogonal", _bool(p.orthogonal) if p.orthogonal is not None else None),
242	        (
243	            "AllowSummation",
244	            _bool(p.allow_summation) if p.allow_summation is not None else None,
245	        ),
246	        # TeX is a LaTeX label; render it as a quoted Mathematica string with
247	        # backslashes escaped ("\\Gamma_U"), else a raw value like \Gamma_U is a
248	        # Mathematica syntax error that aborts the whole M$Parameters block.
249	        ("TeX", _quote(p.tex) if p.tex else None),
250	        ("Description", _quote(p.description) if p.description else None),
251	    ]
252	    return f"  {p.name} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
253	
254	
255	def render_parameters(params: List[Parameter]) -> str:
256	    entries = ",\n".join(_render_parameter(p) for p in params)
257	    return "M$Parameters = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
258	
259	
260	def _render_particle(p: ParticleClass) -> str:
261	    pairs: List[Tuple[str, Optional[str]]] = [
262	        ("ClassName", p.class_name),
263	        ("SelfConjugate", _bool(p.self_conjugate)),
264	        (
265	            "ClassMembers",
266	            ("{" + ", ".join(p.class_members) + "}") if p.class_members else None,
267	        ),
268	        ("Indices", _indices(p.indices) if p.indices else None),
269	        ("FlavorIndex", p.flavor_index),
270	        ("Mass", _mass(p.mass) if p.mass else None),
271	        ("Width", _mass(p.width) if p.width else None),
272	        ("QuantumNumbers",
273	         _qn(p.quantum_numbers) if _additive_qns(p.quantum_numbers or {}) else None),
274	        ("PDG", _pdg(p.pdg) if p.pdg is not None else None),
275	        ("ParticleName", _name_field(p.particle_name) if p.particle_name else None),
276	        (
277	            "AntiParticleName",
278	            _name_field(p.antiparticle_name) if p.antiparticle_name else None,
279	        ),
280	        ("FullName", _name_field(p.full_name) if p.full_name else None),
281	        (
282	            "PropagatorLabel",
283	            _name_field(p.propagator_label) if p.propagator_label else None,
284	        ),
285	        ("PropagatorType", p.propagator_type.value if p.propagator_type else None),
286	        ("PropagatorArrow", p.propagator_arrow.value if p.propagator_arrow else None),
287	        ("Ghost", p.ghost),
288	        ("Goldstone", p.goldstone),
289	        ("Chirality", p.chirality),
290	        ("MajoranaPhase", p.majorana_phase),
291	        (
292	            "WeylComponents",
293	            ("{" + ", ".join(p.weyl_components) + "}") if p.weyl_components else None,
294	        ),
295	        ("Unphysical", _bool(True) if p.unphysical else None),
296	        (
297	            "Definitions",
298	            ("{" + ", ".join(p.definitions) + "}") if p.definitions else None,
299	        ),
300	    ]
301	    return f"  {p.class_label} == " + _assoc(pairs, indent="    ")
302	
303	
304	def render_classes(particles: List[ParticleClass]) -> str:
305	    entries = ",\n".join(_render_particle(p) for p in particles)
306	    return "M$ClassesDescription = {\n" + entries + "\n};"
307	
308	
309	def render_model(model: FeynRulesModel) -> str:
310	    """Render a validated FeynRulesModel to a complete ``.fr`` string."""
311	    sections: List[str] = [render_information(model.info)]
312	
313	    if model.interaction_order_hierarchy:
314	        ih = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_hierarchy)
315	        sections.append("M$InteractionOrderHierarchy = {" + ih + "};")
316	    if model.interaction_order_limit:
317	        il = ", ".join(_interaction_order(t) for t in model.interaction_order_limit)
318	        sections.append("M$InteractionOrderLimit = {" + il + "};")
319	    if model.feynman_gauge is not None:
320	        sections.append(f"FeynmanGauge = {_bool(model.feynman_gauge)};")
321	    if model.vevs:
322	        vv = ", ".join(f"{{{f}, {v}}}" for f, v in model.vevs)
323	        sections.append("M$vevs = {" + vv + "};")
324	
325	    for raw in model.raw_preamble:
326	        sections.append(raw)
327	
328	    if model.index_decls:
329	        sections.append(render_index_decls(model.index_decls))
330	    if model.gauge_groups:
331	        sections.append(render_gauge_groups(model.gauge_groups))
332	    if model.parameters:
333	        # FeynRules auto-declares the mass/width parameters named in each
334	        # particle's Mass/Width spec. Re-declaring them in M$Parameters makes the
335	        # UFO define the name twice, which MadGraph rejects ("name X define
336	        # multiple time"). Drop those duplicates; keep genuine couplings.
337	        reserved = _reserved_mass_width_names(model.particles)
338	        params = [p for p in model.parameters
339	                  if p.name not in reserved or _is_internal_param(p)]
340	        if params:
341	            sections.append(render_parameters(params))
342	    if model.particles:
343	        sections.append(render_classes(model.particles))
344	    for field, expr in model.gauge_xi:
345	        sections.append(f"GaugeXi[{field}] = {expr};")
346	
347	    for raw in model.raw_blocks:
348	        sections.append(raw)
349	
350	    for t in model.lagrangian_terms:
351	        op = ":=" if t.delayed else "="
352	        # Defensive: some (LLM-produced) expressions already carry a leading
353	        # assignment operator ("= ..." or ":= ..."); strip it so we don't emit a
354	        # duplicated operator (e.g. "L := := Block[...]").
355	        rhs = t.expression.lstrip()
356	        for lead in (":=", "="):
357	            if rhs.startswith(lead):
358	                rhs = rhs[len(lead):].lstrip()
359	                break
360	        sections.append(f"{t.name} {op} {rhs};")
361	
362	    env = Environment(
363	        loader=FileSystemLoader(_TEMPLATE_DIR),
364	        autoescape=select_autoescape(enabled_extensions=(), default=False),
365	        keep_trailing_newline=True,
366	    )
367	    template = env.get_template("model.fr.j2")
368	    return template.render(model_name=model.model_name, body="\n\n".join(sections))
369

1	(***************************************************************************************************************)
2	(******                       This is the FeynRules mod-file for the Standard model                       ******)
3	(******                                                                                                   ******)
4	(******     Authors: N. Christensen, C. Duhr, B. Fuks                                                     ******)
5	(******                                                                                                   ******)
6	(****** Choose whether Feynman gauge is desired.                                                          ******)
7	(****** If set to False, unitary gauge is assumed.                                                          ****)
8	(****** Feynman gauge is especially useful for CalcHEP/CompHEP where the calculation is 10-100 times faster. ***)
9	(****** Feynman gauge is not supported in MadGraph and Sherpa.                                              ****)
10	(***************************************************************************************************************)

13	(* *****  Information   ***** *)

22	  Emails       -> {"neil@pa.msu.edu", "claude.duhr@uclouvain.be", "benjamin.fuks@cnrs.in2p3.fr"},

88	  }

173	    PropagatorType   -> C,

731	  generators = {-I/2 g1 IdentityMatrix[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[1], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[2], -I/2 gw PauliSigma[3]};
732	  doublet = Expand[{(-I phi1 - phi2)/Sqrt[2], Phi[2]} /. MR$Definitions /. vev -> 0]; 
733	  doublet0 = {0, vev/Sqrt[2]};
734	  Vectorize[{a_, b_}]:= Simplify[{Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[a]], Sqrt[2] Re[Expand[b]], Sqrt[2] Im[Expand[b]]}/.{Im[_]->0, Re[num_]->num}];
735	  togoldstones := {phi1 -> (GP + GPbar)/Sqrt[2], phi2 -> (-GP + GPbar)/(I Sqrt[2])};

I read the paper, the schema, the renderer and SM.fr. No cached or reference `.fr` file for this model exists in the sandbox, and none was read.

## Model content (from Table X, Eq. 12, Eq. 13)

Four new states, all SU(2)_L singlets in the colour sextet: scalars Φ_u (6,1,1/3), Φ_d (6,1,4/3) with L = −1; Dirac fermions Ψ_u (6,1,−2/3), Ψ_d (6,1,1/3) with L = 0. Hypercharge signs re-derived from the operators: the paper's bilinear `(q^c q')` adds both charges, so Eq. (12) needs Y_Ψq = −Y_qR and Eq. (13) needs Y_Φq = −Y_qR + 1. Both reproduce Table X exactly, so no convention clash with SM.fr (Q = T3 + Y, Y(uR)=2/3, Y(dR)=−1/3, Y(lR)=−1).

Colour structure: J^{sia} = −i ε^{ijk} [t^a_3]^l_j K̄^s_{lk} from Eq. (A18) with √2 L^{ijk} = ε^{ijk} (footnote 8), written with the FeynRules built-ins `Eps`, `T` and `K6bar`, exactly the "existing semi-hard-coded objects" route the paper says it used.

Extra required lines:
- SelfConjugate -> True classes: **none**. All four new classes are complex (distinct antiparticle), so no class carries QuantumNumbers illegally.
- Names used — classes `PhiU`, `PhiD`, `PsiU`, `PsiD`; parameters `MPhiU`, `MPhiD`, `MPsiU`, `MPsiD`, `WPhiU`, `WPhiD`, `WPsiU`, `WPsiD`, `LamPsiU`, `LamPsiD`, `LamPsiUB`, `LamPsiDB`, `LamPhiU`, `LamPhiD`, `kapU`, `kapD`, `kapUB`, `kapDB`, `lamU`, `lamD`; index `Sextet`; term names `LKinPsiU`, `LKinPsiD`, `LKinPhiU`, `LKinPhiD`, `LPsiUG`, `LPsiDG`, `LPsiUB`, `LPsiDB`, `LPhiUG`, `LPhiDG`, `LTotal`. None is a Mathematica built-in, a FeynRules symbol (`HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, `T`, `K6bar`), or an SM.fr name (`Phi`, `H`, `lam`, `G`, `B`, `l`, `uq`, `dq`, ...). No primes or punctuation in any ParticleName.
- Single total Lagrangian: **LTotal** = LKinPsiU + LKinPsiD + LKinPhiU + LKinPhiD + LPsiUG + LPsiDG + LPsiUB + LPsiDB + LPhiUG + LPhiDG. Every other declared term appears in it; no second total is defined; no term is field-free.
- Reference or cached model file read: **none**. Only the paper text, `frmodel.py`, `render.py` and the supplied `SM.fr` were read.

Note on the CC idiom: the barred charge-conjugate is written `CC[uqbar[ff, ii]]` / `CC[dqbar[ff, ii]]` (CC applied to the barred class field with its Generation and Colour indices), which is the FeynRules spelling of `\bar{q^c}`; the bare field is never used where the paper writes q^c.
